etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From Middle English zelose, from Latin zēlōsus, from zēlus + -ōsus, from Ancient Greek ζῆλος (zêlos, “zeal, jealousy”), from ζηλόω (zēlóō, “to emulate, to be jealous”). By surface analysis, zeal +‎ -ous. Doublet of jealous.
senses: Full of zeal; ardent, fervent; exhibiting enthusiasm or strong passion, particularly in matters of religion.
